guarantees.claim: Each wire is continuously assigned the result of the GF(2^2) multiplication function aes_mul_gf2p2 of its respective inputs: mul_b0_c1_inv = aes_mul_gf2p2(b0, c1_inv); mul_q0_c1_inv = aes_mul_gf2p2(q0, c1_inv); mul_b1_c2_inv = aes_mul_gf2p2(b1, c2_inv); mul_q1_c2_inv = aes_mul_gf2p2(q1, c2_inv).

assumptions.claim: Inputs b0, q0, c1_inv, b1, q1, c2_inv must be valid GF(2^2) values; outside the domain the multiplication results are not meaningful.
assumptions.risk: Invalid inputs produce undefined multiplication results, corrupting the inverse computation and potentially breaking the masked S-box security.

uncertain_points.claim: The comment 'Avoid aggressive synthesis optimizations' indicates security intent to preserve these intermediate mask multiplications, but the RTL contains no explicit synthesis keep/dont_touch directive. Synthesis tools may legally merge combinational paths, potentially compromising side-channel resistance.
uncertain_points.cond: when synthesized with any optimization that could merge these nets
uncertain_points.risk: Glitch-based leakage or unintended sharing combination may expose secret key material through power/EM side channels.
